output.headline: Pays Robert Half up to $119,000.00 for contract talent services for the Legal Department
output.summary: Robert Half, Inc., of Oakland, will provide contract talent services to the district's Legal Department, as described in the agreement. The cost is capped at $119,000.00 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Accepts $3,724,125.91 from the Salesforce Foundation, passed through Oakland Public Education Fund
output.summary: The district accepts $3,724,125.91 in funding from the Salesforce Foundation, handled through the Oakland Public Education Fund, to support educational outcomes in the district. The money is spent by program area as set out in the grant agreement. It covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays Star Elevator up to $68,887.80 to install a new pump on the Laurel Elementary elevator
output.summary: Star Elevator, of Belmont, will install a new submersible pump unit on the passenger elevator at Laurel Elementary School so the elevator meets code. The cost is capped at $68,887.80, paid from deferred maintenance funds. The work was scheduled to run from July 1 to October 31, 2026, so it was set to begin before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Sown to Grow up to $232,900.00 for student well-being check-in software and training
output.summary: Sown to Grow, Inc., of Oakland, will provide software licenses, a weekly social-emotional check-in and wellness surveys for students, plus training, coaching and data reports for teachers and principals in all TK-12 schools. The cost is capped at $232,900.00 for August 1, 2026 to June 1, 2027. The start date is before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Window Tints Everything up to $67,488.10 for sun-reflecting window film at four schools
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The official title names three schools (Hoover, Bridges, Sequoia), but the action text also lists Laurel Elementary School.
output.summary: Window Tints Everything, of North Hollywood, will clean and install reflective window film on the south- and west-facing classroom windows most affected by sun at Hoover Elementary, Bridges Academy, Sequoia Elementary and Laurel Elementary. The $67,488.10 limit includes a $6,135.31 contingency. Work was scheduled for July 20 to September 9, 2026, so it began before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $425,000.00 East Bay Community Foundation grant for Oakland Goes Outdoors staff
output.summary: The East Bay Community Foundation, acting for the Robert and Kathryn Riddell Fund, is giving the district $425,000.00 to cover dedicated district salary and staff costs for Oakland Goes Outdoors. The program runs through the Middle Schools Network. The grant covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Accepts a $500,000.00 grant from the Association for Continuing Education for Rudsdale High School
output.summary: The Association for Continuing Education, of Los Altos, is giving the district $500,000.00 to support its learning center program at Rudsdale High School. The money pays for workplace learning coordination, four dual-enrollment classes, staff training and a student leadership elective. The grant covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays LogicTree up to $45,425.50 for a new tip-management system through June 2029
output.summary: LogicTree IT Solutions, of Citrus Heights, will provide a FormsTrackR subscription for managing incoming tips, adding 30 more sites and staff accounts to receive and assign tips. It will also move the district's current HubConnect tips features and data into the new system. The cost is capped at $45,425.50 for July 16, 2026 to June 30, 2029, and the start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Yeah, Art! up to $77,000.00 for after-school music at three middle schools
output.summary: Yeah, Art!, of Oakland, will run after-school music enrichment at Melrose, Montera and Westlake Middle Schools, up to two days a week, for up to 160 students and up to 500 hours of instruction over 30 weeks. It includes up to two student showcases per site. The cost is capped at $77,000.00 for August 3, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and the start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Peninsulators $32,007.00 for sun-reflecting window film at Chabot Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators, Inc., of San Jose, will clean and install reflective window film on the south- and west-facing classroom windows most hit by direct sun at Chabot Elementary School. The lump sum is $32,007.00, including a $2,838.00 contingency. Work was scheduled for July 30 to September 6, 2026, so it began before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Peninsulators $36,200.00 for sun-reflecting window film at East Oakland Pride Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators Inc., of San Jose, will clean and install reflective window film on the south- and west-facing classroom windows most hit by direct sun at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The lump sum is $36,200.00, including a $3,210.00 contingency. Work was scheduled for July 30 to September 6, 2026, so it began before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Peninsulators $20,764.00 for sun-reflecting window film at Cleveland Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators Inc., of San Jose, will prepare and install reflective window film on the south- and west-facing classroom windows most hit by direct sun at Cleveland Elementary School. The lump sum is $20,764.00, including a $1,887.00 contingency. Work was scheduled for July 30 to September 6, 2026, so it began before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Peninsulators $21,476.00 for sun-reflecting window film at Stonehurst Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators Inc., of San Jose, will prepare and install reflective window film in the classrooms most affected by sun at Stonehurst Elementary School. The lump sum is $21,476.00, including a $1,952.00 contingency. Work was scheduled for July 30 to September 6, 2026, so it began before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Awards OBR Electric $648,295.56 to replace the Skyline High School field lights
output.summary: OBR Electric, of Oakland, was the lowest responsible, responsive bidder to install new light poles, underground conduit and a commissioned lighting system for the Skyline High School football field. The $648,295.56 price includes a $120,000.00 contingency. Work is expected to start August 27 and finish by November 19, 2026, within 84 days.

output.headline: Awards Redgwick Construction $816,100.00 for Sequoia Elementary playground and garden upgrades
output.summary: Redgwick Construction Company, of Oakland, was the lowest responsible, responsive bidder to remove old play structures and some asphalt, build nature and garden spaces, prepare for new play structures, plant trees and seal-coat pavement and murals at Sequoia Elementary School. The $816,100.00 price includes an $82,400.00 contingency. Work is expected to run from August 27 to October 30, 2026.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the Board's August 4, 2026 special meeting
output.summary: The Board approves the written minutes of its Special Meeting held on August 4, 2026. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. No money is involved.

output.headline: Pays Prescott Circus Theatre up to $40,000.00 for after-school performing arts at two elementary schools
output.summary: Prescott Circus Theatre, of Oakland, will offer after-school performing arts classes at Piedmont Avenue and Esperanza Elementary Schools, up to two days a week, for up to 80 students and 240 hours of instruction. The cost is capped at $40,000.00 for August 3, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Cantare Con Vivo up to $40,000.00 for after-school music at three campuses
output.summary: Cantare Con Vivo, of Oakland, will provide after-school music classes at Melrose Leadership Academy's Sherman Campus, Horace Mann Elementary and Bridges Academy, up to two days a week at each site. It serves up to 100 students with 480 hours of instruction and up to two showcase performances per site. The cost is capped at $40,000.00 for August 3, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and the start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Climate Pro $46,900.50 for sun-reflecting window film at Horace Mann Elementary
output.summary: Miller Dobbins Family, Inc., doing business as Climate Pro, of Cotati, will clean and install reflective 3M Affinity window film on 498 classroom windows at Horace Mann Elementary School. The lump sum is $46,900.50, including a $4,139.50 contingency. Work was scheduled for July 30 to October 6, 2026, so it began before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Elevate Oakland up to $70,000.00 for music programs at three secondary schools
output.summary: Elevate Oakland will provide up to 500 hours of music instruction for up to 90 students at Castlemont High, Oakland Technical High and Elmhurst Middle School. Classes run two days a week over 30 weeks, with performance opportunities at community events. The cost is capped at $70,000.00 for August 3, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Accepts a $320,000.00 Eat.Learn.Play Foundation grant for food and garden programming
output.summary: The Eat.Learn.Play Foundation, of Oakland, awarded the district $320,000.00 through a grant agreement letter for staffing and hands-on learning in its Environment, Food and Garden Program at the Central Kitchen and Education Center. The grant covers July 23, 2026 through July 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $58,800.00 for structured recess and student leadership at Allendale Elementary
output.summary: HERO, of Oakland, will run a structured recess program at Allendale Elementary School, support a safe and inclusive playground and teach leadership and conflict resolution. Upper-grade students join the daily Young HERO leadership program with monthly workshops. The cost is capped at $58,800.00 for August 10, 2026 to May 25, 2027, and the start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Symphony up to $60,000.00 for after-school music at five elementary schools
schools: Martin Luther King, Jr. Elementary School
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title says Services Agreement 2026-2027, but the action text calls it a Services Agreement 2025-2026 while giving a 2026-2027 service period.
output.summary: Oakland Symphony will teach after-school music classes at Hoover, Garfield, Manzanita SEED, Brookfield and Martin Luther King, Jr. Elementary Schools, twice a week for 30 weeks, for up to 160 students and at least 432 hours of service. The cost is capped at $60,000.00 for August 3, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and the start date is before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Pays up to $800.00 in Bay Area Collaborative membership fees for special education services
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding sets a fee to be paid by the Special Education Local Plan Area (SELPA) for membership in the Bay Area Collaborative. The fee supports services provided by the SELPA that chairs the collaborative. The cost is capped at $800.00 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays Urban Heat Academy up to $150,000.00 for after-school stepping and cultural arts at four sites
output.summary: Urban Heat Academy, of Alameda, will run after-school stepping and cultural arts programs at four school sites, totaling 864 hours of direct service to students. Sessions cover rhythm, movement, choreography, teamwork and leadership, for an estimated 25 to 30 students per site per session. The cost is capped at $150,000.00 for August 27, 2026 to May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Pays EliteGamingLIVE up to $237,709.49 for an online esports hub at 17 middle schools
output.summary: EliteGamingLIVE, Inc., of Columbia, Maryland, will provide an online learning hub where students build gaming skills, explore esports career paths and practice year round. It serves 17 middle school campuses, with up to 60 students per site each season across three seasons. The cost is capped at $237,709.49 for August 26, 2026 to May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Amends Star Academy's special education contract to change class size, calendar and progress report terms
output.summary: This amendment changes three sections of the district's 2026-27 master contract with Star Academy, of San Rafael, a nonpublic, nonsectarian school or agency that provides special education services required by students' Individualized Education Programs. The sections cover class size, calendars and student progress reports. All other terms stay the same, and no new dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost deal with Eagle Ambulance for student EMT ride-along experiences
output.summary: Eagle Ambulance, of San Leandro, will provide ride-along experiences for district students enrolled in the Highway to Work: Emergency Medical Technician program. There is no cost to the district. The agreement covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, so it started before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Approves $1,372,113 in 2025-26 Measure G1 carryover funds for named schools
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text calls the figure the "culminative" amount, which appears to be a misspelling of "cumulative"; the named school is singular ("Named School") while the title says "Named Schools".
output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt a resolution accepting the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendation. It approves carrying over unspent 2025-2026 Measure G1 money, totaling $1,372,113, to the schools named in the resolution. Measure G1 supports teacher retention and middle school improvement.

output.headline: Adopts a resolution to demolish obsolete portable buildings at the former John Swett and Tilden campus
output.summary: This resolution authorizes demolishing obsolete portable buildings and stabilizing the site at the former John Swett Elementary and Tilden Child Development Center campus. It is described as supporting the Facilities Master Plan and the district's asset management strategy. The text states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $15,600 for Board facilitation and governance support

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $15,600.00

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The agreement period begins June 1, 2026, which is before the August 26, 2026 meeting date, so the work may have started before Board approval.
output.summary: The district would hire Eve Gordon of Alameda to provide facilitation, leadership development and governance support to the Board of Education. The contract runs from June 1, 2026 through February 1, 2027 and is paid from the General Purpose fund. The payment cannot exceed $15,600.

output.headline: Approves the written record of the Board's August 12, 2026 regular meeting
output.summary: The Board of Education is asked to formally approve the minutes of its regular meeting held on August 12, 2026. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. Approving them makes them the official record of what happened.

output.headline: Approves amended 2026-27 Measure G1 funding applications for named schools
output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt a resolution accepting the recommendation of the Measure G1 oversight commission. The commission reviews how schools use Measure G1 money, which supports teacher retention and middle school improvement. The resolution approves amended 2026-2027 school year funding applications for the schools named in it. The text does not state dollar amounts.

output.headline: Retains Olson Remcho Law Firm for up to $114,000 a year in legal advice through June 2028
output.summary: The district's General Counsel may use Olson Remcho Law Firm for advice on the Teacher Retention and Educational Programs Replacement Act. The firm may also help with elections, campaign finance, ethics, constitutional and public policy law, and litigation defense, as needed. Fees are capped at $114,000 in a fiscal year for July 20, 2026 to June 30, 2028, and the start date is before this ratification vote.
